subject: [PATCH RFC] NFS: don't wait for writeback on close() with a write delegation

reviews.author: Trond Myklebust
reviews.summary: Reviewer Trond Myklebust questioned the inconsistency in applying congestion control to the WB_SYNC_NONE case and not re-checking for congestion in subsequent loops, suggesting that if congestion control is applied, it should be done consistently throughout the code.
reviews.raw_body:
Urgh...

OK, I've got to stop and ask why commit 2f1f31042ef0 ("nfs: Block on
write congestion") only applies congestion control to the WB_SYNC_NONE
case?

Also, why does it not re-check for congestion in the loops further down
in nfs_writepages where it's adding fuel to the congestion fire?

Put differently: If we're going to apply congestion control, then why
are we not doing so consistently here?

-- 
Trond Myklebust
Linux NFS client maintainer, Hammerspace
trondmy@kernel.org, trond.myklebust@hammerspace.com

reviews.author: Trond Myklebust
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch is likely to cause issues in the pNFS case due to global write congestion wait being used across multiple data servers, each with independent congestion characteristics.
sentiment_signals: patch may not work as intended
reviews.raw_body:
Another note: this is almost certainly completely borked for the pNFS
case, since nfss->write_congestion_wait is global to the metadata
server. In the pNFS case, you can have lots of data servers that have
completely independent congestion characteristics.

-- 
Trond Myklebust
Linux NFS client maintainer, Hammerspace
trondmy@kernel.org, trond.myklebust@hammerspace.com

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch may need a fix due to potential server-wide congestion caused by other files, agreed to re-examine and clean up the code in a future version.
reviews.raw_body:
Alrighty, let me take a look at what we can do to clean this up. Stay
tuned. Thanks for the confirmation!

Cheers,
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

2026-11-23.patch_summary: This patch reverts a change that avoids waiting for writeback on close() when there's a write delegation, and instead suggests switching back to the previous behavior of using filemap_fdatawrite(). The original change was intended to improve performance, but it has some limitations, such as blocking on server-wide congestion caused by other files.
